$comment: Row-key text vectors (D-row-key). Each vector names a table's key columns in primary-key order, a row as Postgres to_jsonb renders it (or as a device writes it), and the pk text every implementation derives from them, byte for byte: one key column gives its component text, several give the JSON array of their component texts in the Postgres jsonb text form. The SQL pack (kizunasync._pk_text) and the Rust engine replay these vectors; a disagreement is a bug in the implementation, never a vector to relax.

vectors.name: a uuid key is the lowercase hyphenated uuid
an integer key is its plain decimal
a negative integer key keeps its minus sign
an integer key sent as a decimal string is that string
a text key is the text unchanged
a single text key is never escaped, even when it reads as JSON
a composite key is a JSON array of strings joined by comma and space
a composite key follows the key column order, not the row order
a composite component escapes a quote, a backslash, and a newline
a composite component escapes U+0001 as lowercase hex and keeps non-ASCII
a composite component uses the short escapes for tab, return, form feed, and backspace
a composite key mixes a uuid and text
